comparator.name: Clinical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The regulations allocate 150 EC to the fixed first five semesters. The final semester combines 15 EC of elective courses with the 15 EC Societal Challenge. The project requires all first-year credits and at least 30 EC of second-year study.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Health and disease across molecular, physiological and behavioural systems
Healthcare systems, social change and the relationship between care and society
Population, environmental and One Health perspectives on prevention

questions: How do biological, behavioural and social systems interact in health and disease?
How should technology and intervention be evaluated and used responsibly in future healthcare?
How can prevention, policy and environmental change improve human, animal and population health?

candidates.label: Health technology, data and responsible innovation
Public health, prevention and healthy environments

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme’s integrated health-and-disease, cross-disciplinary and care-and-society interests. Two further coherent directions remain. Explicit interests in technology, future healthcare and ethical challenges support a health-technology, data and AI route; explicit interests in prevention, epidemics, greener healthcare, living environments and population health support a public-health, policy and society route. All three schedules are feasible and substantively distinct: the closest and technology routes share 13 courses, the closest and public-health routes share 11, and the technology and public-health routes share 6. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached.

alternatives.label: Health, disease & society
alternatives.labelReason: The route integrates the strongest available UCR biomedical, life-science, neuroscience, psychology, population-health, sociology and research-methods sequence. The label names that broad academic combination without implying clinical training or the comparator’s formal medical, pharmaceutical and veterinary integration.
alternatives.concept: Study how biological systems function and how disease disrupts them. Combine anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and pharmacology with psychology, epidemiology and social context.
progression: Foundations in life science and behaviour precede anatomy, molecular biology and laboratory work. Physiology and biochemistry support subsequent pathology, pharmacology and disease study. Epidemiology and sociology add population context.

alternatives.label: Health technology, data & AI
alternatives.labelReason: The route retains a substantial biomedical and behavioural core while adding programming, data science, machine learning, medical imaging, robotics and AI ethics. The label states this interdisciplinary direction without claiming a dedicated clinical-technology qualification.
alternatives.concept: Combine biomedical study with programming, data analysis and AI. Explore how imaging, modelling and robotics can inform health-related questions, alongside the ethical issues these tools raise.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes dedicated epidemiology, anatomy, molecular cell biology, biochemistry, infection and immunity, neurobiology, abnormal psychology, medical and health psychology, sociology, psychodiagnostics and lifespan psychology. It adds programming, mathematical methods, introductory and advanced data science, machine learning, computer vision, databases, algorithms, linear algebra, robotics and AI ethics. Thirteen courses are shared and eleven differ, shifting the organising logic from broad biomedical and behavioural study to computation and emerging healthcare technology.
progression: Programming, data analysis and mathematics precede later modelling, robotics and neural networks. Linear algebra precedes robotics, and physiology and laboratory work supply biomedical context for later imaging and research.

alternatives.label: Public health, policy & society
alternatives.labelReason: The route centres epidemiology, prevention, biopsychosocial health, research, ethics, economics, organisational leadership, sociology, environmental governance and public communication. The label accurately describes an interdisciplinary public-health direction without claiming a professional public-health or healthcare qualification.
alternatives.concept: Study what shapes health across populations. Combine epidemiology, health psychology and research methods with public economics, environmental justice and communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the anatomy, cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory, pathology, immunology, mechanisms-of-disease, pharmacology, neurobiology, cognitive-neuroscience and psychodiagnostics sequence. It adds ethics, qualitative research, public and behavioural economics, organisational and diversity leadership, modern and contemporary sociology, sustainability governance, international-relations theory and persuasive communication. Eleven courses are shared with the closest match and six with the technology route. Its organising logic is prevention, populations, institutions and policy rather than biomedical mechanisms or technology development.
progression: Introductory sociology precedes later social theory. Epidemiology, qualitative inquiry and statistics support public policy, health psychology, evidence synthesis and later environmental justice.

blocks: Both study normal physiological regulation, including homeostasis. Utrecht also examines disruptions to that balance.
Both study anatomy and organ systems. Utrecht compares development and structure across species.
Both study drug action, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Utrecht considers treatment across patient groups.
Both address microbes and infectious disease. UCR also develops the mechanisms of immune defence.
Both examine organ-system disease. Utrecht applies clinical reasoning to human and animal cases.
Both examine cells, signalling and molecular processes. Utrecht applies these to human and animal health.
Both examine ageing and later life. UCR focuses on psychological development across the lifespan.
Both examine mental health and behaviour. Utrecht integrates medical, pharmaceutical and veterinary perspectives.
Both use data and statistical inference to investigate empirical questions. The applications and software differ.
Utrecht studies early human and animal development in a dedicated course.
Utrecht includes three short placements that introduce students to professional practice.
Utrecht examines professional ethical dilemmas in clinical settings.
Utrecht sets aside 15 EC for student-selected electives.
Utrecht requires the 15 EC Societal Challenge. The optional UCR research element appears alongside it and sits outside the course schedules.
Both examine population health and the effects of environmental conditions. Utrecht also considers animal health.
Both use philosophical reasoning to examine ethical questions. Utrecht applies it to care and health.
Both study techniques for analysing images. Utrecht places imaging alongside other technologies in medicine, pharmacy and veterinary care.

notes.text: Utrecht combines medicine, pharmacy and veterinary perspectives with placements and a final project. The UCR options explore related biomedical, behavioural, population-health and technology questions through Liberal Arts and Sciences.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Dutch-taught Clinical Sciences degree, Zorg, gezondheid en samenleving, connects medicine, pharmacy and veterinary science with questions about health and society.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR examples focus on health and disease, health technology and data, or public health and policy.
